newsitem.title: USA: Ross expected to return to Mideast next week.
newsitem.headline: Ross expected to return to Mideast next week.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will return to the Middle East, probably late next week, to resume mediating Israeli-Palestinian talks on the West Bank town of Hebron, the State Department said on Friday.

Ross flew back to Washington on Tuesday after three weeks of talks that failed to nail down an agreement for Israeli troops to make a partial withdrawal in Hebron, as they are required to do under past Israeli-Palestinian accords.
The envoy said on Wednesday he could go back to the region, but left open the possibility that he might not if lower-level technical discussions between the parties were successful.
But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Friday that "sometime after our own (presidential) elections next Tuesday, probably late next week, Dennis will be returning to the region."
He said Ross would "take up again, in person, his conversations with the Israelis and Palestinians to try to bring to closure the Hebron redeployment discussions."
Ross left the Middle East after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat departed on a European tour on last Monday. Arafat has now returned to his Gaza headquarters.

Ross and other U.S. officials have expressed confidence the Hebron talks will be successful. Hebron, where some 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Arabs, would be the seventh West Bank city where Israeli troops have redeployed under Palestinian self-rule accords.
According to Israeli and Palestinian officials, the main sticking points are Israeli rights of "hot pursuit" into PLO-controlled areas, and the type of arms to be carried by Palestinian police.
